title: 2013 HMMT November Guts Problem 20
statement:
There exist unique nonnegative integers \(A, B\) between 0 and 9 , inclusive, such that

\[(1001 \cdot A+110 \cdot B)^{2}=57,108,249\]

Find \(10 \cdot A+B\).

solutions.text: 75 We only need to bound for \(A B 00\); in other words, \(A B^{2} \leq 5710\) but \((A B+1)^{2} \geq 5710\). A quick check gives \(A B=75\). (Lots of ways to get this...)
